items.title: Leiden scientists 3D-print microrobots that swim without a brain

featured_image.name: Microrobots swim and steer with no brain, sensors, or software

items.description: Researchers at Leiden University have built microscopic 3D-printed robots that can swim, navigate obstacles, and adapt to their surroundings — all without sensors, software, or any form of electronic brain. The findings, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences on March 26, represent a departure from conventional approaches to microrobotics, where machines typically rely on external control signals or onboard computation to function.[1][2]

items.title: ASU method maps protein motion in hours, not months

featured_image.name: ASU researchers pioneer technique to study Brownian motion at micro scale |  ASU News

items.description:
Scientists at Arizona State University have developed a method to extract the slow, sweeping motions of proteins from short computer simulations, a breakthrough published on March 26 in Science Advances that could reshape how researchers design drugs, tackle cancer, and combat antibiotic resistance.[1][2]

The technique, called frequency-selective anharmonic (FRESEAN) mode analysis, identifies low-frequency vibrations — the deep, slow rhythms that govern how a protein bends, twists, and shifts between functional shapes — without relying on the simplifying assumptions that limited previous approaches. "We resurrected a long-standing idea that conformational transitions in proteins are tied to low-frequency vibrations," said Associate Professor Matthias Heyden, who leads the research group in ASU's School of Molecular Sciences. "We developed a method to identify these vibrations through natural fluctuations caused by molecular collisions".[2][1]

items.title: IAEA says no radiation risk after strikes hit Iranian nuclear sites

featured_image.name: Health risks from Israeli strikes on Iran's nuclear sites ...

items.description: The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed on Friday that strikes on several Iranian facilities, including the Khondab heavy water production plant and the Khuzestan Steel Factory, posed no radiation risk, even as the agency's chief warned that continued military activity near the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant could trigger a catastrophic radiological accident.

items.title: All-perovskite tandem solar cell hits 29.76% efficiency

featured_image.name: Perovskite solar cells maintain 95% of power conversion efficiency after  1,100 hours at 85°C with new molecular coating

items.description: A burst of recent breakthroughs is bringing perovskite solar cells closer to commercial viability, as research teams in Germany and China have independently developed strategies to boost both efficiency and resilience in these next-generation photovoltaic devices.

items.title: G7 ministers press Iran to reopen Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iran holding world’s economy ‘hostage’ with Strait of Hormuz closure – Cooper

items.description:
UK Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper declared Thursday that Iran "cannot hold the global economy hostage" as she joined counterparts from the Group of Seven nations at the Abbaye des Vaux-de-Cernay outside Paris to address the escalating crisis in the Middle East.[1][2]

Speaking ahead of the two-day gathering, Cooper called for "a swift resolution that reaches regional stability and security and opens the Strait of Hormuz," the vital maritime chokepoint through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply passed before Iran's effective blockade began in late February. The meeting, hosted by French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot under France's G7 presidency, also drew U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who arrived in France overnight and was expected to discuss Iran over lunch on Friday.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: IAEA warns strikes near Iran’s Bushehr Plant risk radiological crisis

featured_image.name: IAEA: Projectile strikes premises of Iran's Bushehr nuclear ...

items.description:
The International Atomic Energy Agency sounded its most urgent alarm yet over the safety of Iran's Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant on Thursday, warning that damage to the operational facility "could result in a major radiological accident affecting a large area in Iran and beyond," as military strikes continue to land near the site during the ongoing US-Israeli campaign against Iran.

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi posted the warning on X, reiterating his "deep concern" about repeated strikes near the plant — Iran's only operational nuclear power station, located on the Persian Gulf coast — and calling on all parties to exercise "maximum restraint". He stressed the importance of adhering to the IAEA's seven-pillar framework for ensuring nuclear safety during armed conflict.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: IRGC urges civilians to flee areas near US forces as Trump extends Hormuz deadline

featured_image.name: IRGC warns civilians to avoid areas with US troops - Caliber.Az

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Friday urged civilians across the Middle East to immediately evacuate areas near American military positions, issuing the warning as the month-old war between the United States, Israel, and Iran showed no signs of abating despite a new extension of President Trump's deadline for Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: US land mines found near Shiraz kill civilians in first such deployment in decades

featured_image.name: Evidence Points to US Scattering Mines over Iranian Village - bellingcat

items.description: Images circulating on social media show what weapons experts have identified as American-made anti-tank land mines scattered across a residential area near Shiraz in southern Iran, in what appears to be the first confirmed deployment of US mines in more than two decades. At least one civilian has been killed and several others wounded after handling the devices, which Iranian state media described as resembling canned food.

items.title: Medvedev warns nuclear conflict between Israel and Iran is now 'inevitable'

featured_image.name: Russia's Medvedev says world should be alarmed if nuclear ...

items.description: Dmitry Medvedev, Russia's deputy chairman of the Security Council, warned on Friday that the U.S.-led war against Iran has made a nuclear conflict between Israel and Iran "inevitable in some form," as Western intelligence reports indicate Moscow is nearing the completion of drone shipments to Tehran — marking the first known transfer of lethal Russian military aid to Iran since the war began.

items.title: Poland's Tusk warns of imminent escalation in Iran war

featured_image.name: Escalation in Middle East possible in coming days, Polish PM ...

items.description:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned on Friday that the war in the Middle East could intensify in the coming days, citing intelligence shared by allied nations as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran nears the one-month mark.

"I have reasons to believe, also based on information we've received from our allies, that stabilization is unlikely in the coming days. On the contrary, a new escalation may occur," Tusk told reporters, according to Reuters, as carried by The Times of Israel.[1]

items.title: Trump demands Iran reopen Strait of Hormuz for peace deal

featured_image.name: Trump Again Pushes Republicans to 'Terminate' the Filibuster

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Friday urged Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as a condition for any peace deal — and in doing so, jokingly referred to the contested waterway as the "Strait of Trump."

"They have to open up the Strait of Trump — I mean Hormuz," Trump said at the Saudi-backed FII Priority Summit in Miami Beach. "Excuse me, I'm so sorry. Such a terrible mistake." He predicted the media would seize on the remark but added, "there's no accidents with me, not too many." Trump drew a parallel to his earlier executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America" shortly after returning to office.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran fires cluster munitions at Tel Aviv, killing one

featured_image.name: Tel Aviv residents assess damage after Iranian missile strike kills one

items.description: A man in his 60s was killed and at least two others injured in the Tel Aviv metropolitan area late Friday night after Iran launched a cluster munition missile at central Israel, capping a day of dramatic escalation in the month-old war. The fatal strike came hours after Israel attacked two Iranian nuclear facilities for the first time in the conflict — and as at least 10 American service members were wounded in a separate Iranian missile attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Saudi Arabia urges US to intensify military campaign against Iran

featured_image.name: An uncrowned king: Saudi Arabia's Prince Mohammed takes the ...

items.description:
Saudi Arabia has called on the United States to intensify its military campaign against Iran and is weighing whether to enter the conflict directly, according to a Saudi intelligence source who confirmed the kingdom's behind-the-scenes role in shaping the nearly month-long war.

The intelligence source, speaking to The Guardian, corroborated a New York Times report that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has urged President Donald Trump in a series of recent conversations not to wind down the US-Israeli military operation against Iran, framing it as a "historic opportunity" to reshape the Middle East. The crown prince has pressed Trump to target Iran's energy infrastructure and even advocated for ground operations, including a potential seizure of Kharg Island, the hub of Iran's oil exports.[1][2][3]

items.title: US confirms killing of IRGC Navy chief Tangsiri in Bandar Abbas strike

featured_image.name: Israel Says It Killed IRGC Navy Commander Responsible for Blocking Strait

items.description:
Israel announced on Thursday that its military killed Rear Admiral Alireza Tangsiri, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy, in an overnight airstrike on the Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas. The strike also killed Behnam Rezaei, head of the IRGC Navy's intelligence directorate, according to the Israel Defense Forces.[1][2]

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the killing in a video statement. "We continue to forcefully strike the targets of the Iranian terrorist regime," Netanyahu said. "Last night, we eliminated the Commander of the IRGC Navy. This man had a great deal of blood on his hands; he was also the one who led the closure of the Strait of Hormuz." Defense Minister Israel Katz described the operation as a "precise and lethal operation" and warned remaining IRGC members: "The IDF will hunt you down and eliminate you one by one."[3][4][5]

U.S. Central Command confirmed Tangsiri's death hours later. Admiral Brad Cooper, CENTCOM commander, called on those serving in the IRGC Navy to "abandon their post and return home to avoid further risk of unnecessary injury or death," according to Gulf News.[6]

items.title: Mexico says 40,000 of 130,000 missing may be alive

featured_image.name: Mexico believes thousands of country's 130,000 missing people could still  be alive | The Independent

items.description: President Claudia Sheinbaum on Friday presented a long-awaited government report on Mexico's disappearance crisis, revealing that 130,178 people remain listed as disappeared over the past two decades, while acknowledging that a poorly maintained national database riddled with gaps, duplications, and missing data has hampered search efforts for years.

items.title: Mediators say Iran never requested strike pause Trump cited

featured_image.name: Trump says US will extend 'pause' on targeting Iranian energy plants  through April 6 - AOL

items.description: Mediators involved in efforts to end the U.S.-Iran war told The Wall Street Journal that Iran has not requested a 10-day pause on strikes against its energy infrastructure, directly contradicting President Trump's claim that the extension was made "as per Iranian Government request." The mediators also said Tehran has yet to deliver a final response to a 15-point American peace proposal aimed at ending the conflict, now in its fourth week.[1][2]

items.title: Rapper Balendra Shah sworn in as Nepal's youngest PM

featured_image.name: Shah sworn in as Nepal's prime minister -Xinhua

items.description:
Balendra Shah, a 35-year-old rapper-turned-politician popularly known as "Balen," was sworn in as Nepal's prime minister on Friday, becoming the youngest leader in the country's democratic history and the first from the Madhesi community of the southern plains to hold the office. President Ram Chandra Paudel administered the oath at the presidential residence in Kathmandu.[1][2][3]

Shah wore skin-tight trousers, a matching jacket, his signature black Nepali cloth cap, and sunglasses to the ceremony, according to Reuters. On the eve of his swearing-in, he posted a new music video on Facebook stressing patriotism: "Nepal is not scared this time, the heart is full of red blood ... laughter and happiness will reach every household this time," he sang.[1]

items.title: Trump presses Saudi Arabia on Abraham Accords at Miami summit

featured_image.name: Trump Presses Saudis to Recognize Israel as He Defends Iran ...

items.description: President Donald Trump delivered the closing address Friday at the Saudi-backed Future Investment Initiative summit in Miami Beach, using the platform to once again press Saudi Arabia to normalize relations with Israel by joining the Abraham Accords — a call he has made repeatedly since his 2025 visit to Riyadh, where he described the prospect as his "dream".[1][2]

items.title: MIT's VibeGen AI designs proteins by how they move

featured_image.name: MIT engineers design proteins by their motion, not just ...

items.description: MIT engineers have developed an AI model called VibeGen that designs proteins based on how they move rather than how they look, a advance that could reshape drug development, materials science, and synthetic biology. The work, published March 24 in the journal Matter, represents the first time scientists can specify a target pattern of motion and have an AI system generate a protein sequence to match it.[1]

items.title: Iranian strike injures 10 US troops at Saudi base

featured_image.name: U.S. military refueling plane crashes in Iraq | PBS News

items.description:
An Iranian missile and drone attack struck Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia on Friday, injuring 10 American service members and damaging multiple U.S. refueling aircraft, according to The Wall Street Journal, citing U.S. and Arab officials. Two of the wounded troops sustained serious injuries, the officials said.[1][2]

The injured personnel were inside a building on the base when it was hit. At least one missile and several drones struck the facility, which serves as a logistics and operational hub for U.S. forces in the region.[1]
